title: VP of Product Management

role_match.role_rationale_from_stage3: This role owns Canon's large-format printer product portfolio strategy, including the Colorado M-series, Arizona flatbed printers, and imagePROGRAF lines. They are responsible for product differentiation, competitive positioning, and ensuring Canon's printers deliver on durability and quality promises to customers. Tedlar directly addresses their KPIs: (1) Product differentiation - partnering with Tedlar provides a premium overlaminate recommendation that extends the durability claims Canon makes for UVgel technology and vehicle wrap applications; (2) Customer success metrics - Tedlar's 12-20+ year outdoor lifespan and UV protection reduce warranty claims and customer complaints about fading/cracking on prints from Canon equipment; (3) Market positioning - Canon emphasizes quality and durability (3M MCS Warranty certification, weather-resistant media) and Tedlar enables them to offer customers a complete solution for extreme durability applications. Given Canon's active product launches (Colorado XL-series debut, M-series enhancements) and trade show presence showcasing outdoor/vehicle graphics capabilities, this role would care about specifying protective films that protect Canon's brand reputation for quality and help customers achieve the longest-lasting results.

engagement_strategy.scope_and_authority: [Name] oversees strategic direction for Canon's large-format printer portfolio, including the Colorado M-series (UVgel technology), Arizona flatbed printers, and imagePROGRAF product families. This is a strategic role with influence over product positioning, go-to-market strategy, competitive differentiation, and ecosystem partnerships (media, substrates, protective films). They likely report to a C-level executive (CMO or SVP of Business Units) and manage product managers responsible for specific printer lines. Key decisions include: which partner products to recommend or certify with Canon equipment, how to position Canon against HP and Epson in durability-sensitive segments, and how to address customer pain points around outdoor performance and warranty claims.
engagement_strategy.relevant_use_cases: Given Canon's Colorado M-series emphasis on vehicle wraps and the Arizona series focus on architectural signage, [Name] would care most about: (1) Vehicle wrap protection - Tedlar's graffiti resistance and UV protection directly complement Canon's marketing claims about UVgel durability in harsh conditions, enabling Canon customers to confidently bid on fleet graphics knowing the wrap will survive 12-20 years; (2) Outdoor signage overlaminates - Canon's customers producing outdoor signs with Arizona flatbeds need protective films that won't yellow or crack, validating Canon's quality positioning and reducing field failures; (3) Architectural graphics - Canon promotes soft signage and building facade applications where Tedlar's weather resistance (-70°F to 230°F) and mold resistance enable installations that outlast competitive solutions. These use cases help [Name]'s team sell more printers by offering customers a complete system solution rather than just hardware.
engagement_strategy.personal_stakes: [Name] likely owns KPIs including product revenue growth, market share in target segments (vehicle wraps, architectural graphics), customer satisfaction scores, and competitive win rates against HP Latex and Epson SureColor. Personally, they care about reducing warranty claims and support escalations tied to print durability failures, as these erode Canon's premium brand positioning and increase service costs. Tedlar solves a strategic problem: Canon can confidently recommend a protective film that matches their equipment's quality promise, reducing the risk that customer complaints about fading or cracking reflect poorly on Canon printers. Additionally, with Canon's recent Colorado XL-series launch and M-series enhancements, [Name] needs differentiation angles to justify premium pricing versus competitors—Tedlar becomes a value-add recommendation that helps Canon's sales teams close higher-margin deals in demanding applications.
engagement_strategy.timing_factors: Canon is title sponsor of PRINTING United Expo 2025 (October in Orlando) where they're showcasing the Colorado XL-series global debut and promoting vehicle graphics and architectural applications. This creates a natural timing hook: [Name] is actively preparing messaging and partner ecosystem recommendations for this major industry event. Additionally, Canon's recent product launches (Colorado M-series enhancements in April 2025, XL-series announcement in November 2025) indicate active product portfolio optimization cycles where new partner specifications and customer success stories are being developed. Canon's emphasis on 3M MCS Warranty certification and water-resistant media rated for 6+ months outdoors suggests ongoing efforts to strengthen durability credentials—making NOW an ideal time to introduce Tedlar as a certified protective film recommendation that extends outdoor lifespan claims from months to decades.

personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Position Tedlar as the missing piece that extends Canon's durability story from 6 months to 12-20 years, enabling [Name] to differentiate Colorado and Arizona printers as the choice for customers who demand extreme outdoor performance without compromising on Canon's quality reputation

personalization_hooks.hook: As title sponsor of PRINTING United Expo 2025 showcasing the Colorado XL-series debut, Canon's product team is preparing ecosystem partner recommendations for vehicle wrap and architectural graphics applications
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Reference Canon's upcoming trade show presence and suggest a brief conversation about how Tedlar could enhance Canon's booth messaging and customer recommendations for premium outdoor applications—framing this as a strategic partnership discussion rather than a vendor pitch

personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Lead with competitive differentiation: while competitors focus on ink technology alone, Canon could offer customers a validated system solution (printer + protective film) that guarantees decades of outdoor performance—turning Tedlar into a strategic advantage that helps [Name]'s team win deals in high-value fleet graphics and architectural facade segments

recommended_approach: Lead with strategic partnership angle focused on product differentiation and Canon's upcoming trade show presence. Frame Tedlar as enabling Canon to extend their durability claims from months to decades, helping [Name] justify premium pricing and win competitive deals in vehicle wraps and architectural graphics. Avoid technical specs in the opening—instead emphasize how Tedlar solves [Name]'s strategic challenge of differentiating Canon's portfolio in a crowded large-format printer market.
